task: Horizon 13 of the agent-agnostic-browser-bridge project (roadmap rev1 after a REPLAN): add viewport-default and single-element (CDP clip rect, element addressed by a findElement CSS-locator ref) screenshots to the standalone tools/chrome-bridge tool, extending the existing captureTab action in place across the parity surface with a flat too-large result-size guard, closed by a mandatory live-Chrome head-to-head verification. Full-page (captureBeyondViewport) capture was in the original rev0 scope but was dropped after a live phase-0 probe proved it non-functional on the deliberately-unfocused sandbox tab.

analysis.objective: Ship one more browser-control capability in the standalone tools/chrome-bridge tool - viewport-default and single-element (CSS-locator-ref-addressed, CDP clip-rect) screenshots of the dedicated unfocused sandbox tab - as a single atomic change across the established parity surface, closed by a mandatory live-Chrome verification. Full-page / beyond-viewport capture is out of this horizon: a live phase-0 probe on 2026-09-04 proved it non-functional on the unfocused sandbox tab.
analysis.successDefinition: Done means all of the following hold: (1) one atomic change extends the screenshot capability so a caller can request a capture of a single element addressed by the same CSS-locator ref shape findElement returns, with the existing viewport-only behaviour preserved as the default; full-page / beyond-viewport capture is explicitly NOT in this horizon (the live phase-0 probe on 2026-09-04 proved Page.captureScreenshot({captureBeyondViewport:true}) hangs past the 15s withDebuggerSession cap or errors CDP -32000 on the deliberately-unfocused sandbox tab and never returns an image); (2) the change lands consistently across every parity-surface member the recent horizons touch - the per-action Params/Result interfaces in protocol/types.ts, both Record<PageAction, ...> mapped types, the raw + guarded handler maps in extension/page-actions.ts, the TOOL_CATALOG entry in mcp/tool-catalog.ts, the affected unit tests, and the README prose/manual-e2e step - with no drift (a missing consumer is a tsc error), and PAGE_ACTIONS stays at 20 (the shape changes in place, not via a new action); (3) failure shapes are explicit and non-throwing where the precedent is non-throwing: element selector matches nothing, element has zero/na box, relay/tab unavailable, and an over-large image are each defined result outcomes, not unhandled hangs or crashes; (4) the returned image stays within MCP result-size limits via a documented flat too-large guard carrying measured bytes plus a named ceiling constant (viewport PNG was ~275KB per h4), and the result carries width/height/clipped metadata to be cross-checked; (5) no new manifest permission is added (debugger is already granted); (6) npm run verify for the tools/chrome-bridge package is green (tsc --noEmit, eslint --max-warnings 0, vitest) and boky's own extension/bridge/verify pipeline is untouched; (7) a MANDATORY live head-to-head runs in a fresh post-rebuild MCP session against a real large below-the-fold element, cross-checked against a CDP evaluatePage getBoundingClientRect measurement (devicePixelRatio reconciled) per the horizon-12 precedent - the element image dimensions track the measured rect - and is recorded as a dated Verified README block; an honest MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING note is an acceptable close if the live environment is unavailable, a hand-waved pass is not.
assumptions: The slice is delivered by extending the existing captureTab capability in place - CaptureTabParams gains a required-with-default two-value mode field (visible viewport | element) and an elementRef field, CaptureTabResult gains width/height/clipped and a too-large marker - keeping PAGE_ACTIONS at 20, mirroring the h12 decision that a result/param shape may change in place rather than via a new action.

The element is addressed by the same self-contained CSS-locator string findElement/clickElement already accept (h12 decision) - never a CDP backend node id, opaque handle, XPath, or index into a prior result set.

Element capture uses CDP Page.captureScreenshot({ clip: { x, y, width, height, scale } }) with the element rect measured via the post-h9 CDP read path (evaluatePage / Runtime.evaluate getBoundingClientRect); this stays within the h6 decision that CDP is used only for the captureVisibleTab-family gap via Page.captureScreenshot.
The capture reuses per-command withDebuggerSession attach/detach (15s cap) with no persistent CDP session, consistent with the h10 scroll decision.

The result is still returned as a data:image/png;base64,... dataUrl surfaced to MCP as an image content block for a real capture, and as a text/error block for a structured non-image outcome (too-large / element-not-found / zero-area).
Verification is Claude-Code-only (h4 decision), live signed-in Chrome, in a fresh MCP session started after the extension rebuild + reload.

The phase-0 probe (rev0) already proved clip capture composites a below-the-fold element on the unfocused sandbox tab, so the narrowed horizon has no remaining feasibility gate - only the standard live head-to-head.
risks: A clip PNG of a very large element can still be multiple hundred KB of base64 - past the ~275KB viewport measurement - so without the flat too-large guard the capability can ship an oversized payload; the guard's ceiling constant and behaviour (return a defined too-large outcome, no downscale) is the roadmap's chosen answer.

Large-image CDP encode of a big element clip may approach the 15s withDebuggerSession cap; the per-command attach/detach lifecycle and timeout must still clean up (the h10 hang + orphaned-attachment failure is the precedent to avoid).

Element capture needs a bbox-measurement round-trip before the capture; a per-command detach between the measure session and the capture session can race scroll position or lifecycle state, yielding a clipped or offset image.

clip interacts with device-scale-factor / emulation overrides - the returned image may not match measured CSS-pixel dimensions unless devicePixelRatio (2 on the sandbox tab) is reconciled explicitly, weakening the mandatory cross-check.

Live verification is repeatedly blocked in this project by relay-down or a frozen MCP tool catalog (h9, h11, h12); the horizon may again end MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING and need a --retry in a later fresh session.

An element selector that matches nothing, matches a display:none / zero-area node, or matches an off-screen node needs a defined non-throwing outcome; picking error vs a structured {captured:false}-style result inconsistently with the codebase's existing non-throwing precedents is a latent inconsistency.
analysis.domainShapeReason: The work is browser-automation machinery - extending a Chrome extension CDP screenshot path and its MCP/protocol parity surface - with no business entities, rules, or workflows a domain expert would recognize.
outOfScope: Full-page / beyond-viewport (captureBeyondViewport) screenshots - dropped from this horizon after the rev0 phase-0 live probe proved Page.captureScreenshot({captureBeyondViewport:true}) hangs past the 15s cap or errors CDP -32000 on the deliberately-unfocused sandbox tab; deferred behind a 'briefly render the sandbox tab' prerequisite, its own future horizon.
A scroll-and-stitch client-side full-page fallback - a different mechanism, its own replanned approach, not part of this slice.
Adding a general focus / briefly render the sandbox tab capability - the prerequisite that full-page capture now sits behind; its own horizon, not this one.
Capturing network response bodies for text/JSON (blocker #4) - a separate deferred capability.
clickElement / clickAt by visible text or ARIA role and a fuller synthetic pointer/keyboard event sequence (blocker #5) - a separate deferred slice.
Reviving the horizon-5 DOM page-model / bounding-box snapshot action - planned-but-never-executed and possibly superseded by h12 findElement; not this horizon's slice.
Deleting the dead active-tab surface (queryActiveTab / captureVisibleTab / NO_ACTIVE_TAB / redundant activeTab permission) - its own horizon.
Verifying the capability from Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, or Cursor - the h4 decision binds all hand-verification to Claude Code for the life of the project.
PDF export, JPEG/quality knobs, or other CDP capture formats/options beyond png + clip - not asked for; format proliferation is speculative.
Migrating boky's own extension/relay/MCP onto the chrome-bridge tool - the vision's h1 decision forbids it.
Changing the MCP result-rendering layer to add a generic size guard for all tools - any size bound added here is scoped to the screenshot result; a cross-tool cap is a separate open question.

Downscale-and-retry / re-capture-at-lower-scale behaviour for an oversized screenshot payload - per the rev0 user redirect the size guard stays flat: an oversized base64 payload returns a defined non-throwing too-large outcome.

discoveryFindings.finding: Page.captureScreenshot({captureBeyondViewport:true}) on the deliberately-unfocused sandbox tab (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromium_(web_browser), scrollHeight ~9271-10194, innerHeight 772, dpr 2) hung 17105ms past the 15s withDebuggerSession cap and wedged the Page.captureScreenshot path until reloadTab recovered it (Runtime.evaluate/chrome.tabs unaffected); a retry errored CDP -32000 'Unable to capture screenshot' in 3847ms. Never returned an image.
discoveryFindings.implication: Full-page / beyond-viewport capture is infeasible in the unfocused sandbox tab and is dropped from horizon 13; deferred behind a 'briefly render the sandbox tab' prerequisite (outOfScope).

discoveryFindings.finding: Page.captureScreenshot({clip:{x,y,width,height,scale}}) on the same unfocused sandbox tab returned a PNG cropped to exactly a genuinely below-the-fold element (table.wikitable at y=4459.77, scrollY 0, never scrolled into view) in 2058ms with a clean debugger auto-detach.
discoveryFindings.implication: Single-element clip capture is feasible on the unfocused sandbox tab with no render-pass prerequisite; it is the retained capability for this horizon and needs no separate feasibility gate.

discoveryFindings.finding: CaptureTabParams is `{ readonly _?: never }` (no args) and CaptureTabResult is `{ readonly dataUrl: string }` (a data:image/png;base64,... URL), in src/protocol/types.ts. Both are registered in the PageActionParams and PageActionResults maps (lines ~192 and ~426). The rev0 probe shim temporarily added captureBeyondViewport?: boolean + clip?: {...} - both must be removed and replaced by the mode/elementRef shape.
discoveryFindings.implication: An element screenshot that reuses captureTab's shape adds the mode/elementRef fields to CaptureTabParams and width/height/clipped/too-large metadata to CaptureTabResult; the probe-only captureBeyondViewport field is deleted.

discoveryFindings.finding: In src/extension/page-actions.ts the raw handler was `captureTab: async () => { const tabId = await sandboxTab.resolveTabId(); const dataUrl = await captureDebugger.captureScreenshot(tabId); return { result: { dataUrl } }; }` wrapped as `captureTab: guard(raw.captureTab)`. The rev0 probe shim added param reading + a numeric clip check. A top-of-file comment said captureTab was deliberately uncapped and large-PNG presentation was 'the MCP server's decision (a later phase)'.
discoveryFindings.implication: Element support means the raw handler reads and validates params (mode + elementRef); pageActionHandlers already receives `captureDebugger: DebuggerPorts` so the clip CDP method is wired through that existing port object; the flat size guard lands in this handler.

discoveryFindings.finding: TOOL_CATALOG.captureTab in src/mcp/tool-catalog.ts was `{ description: '...Takes no arguments.', inputSchema: NO_ARGS }`. The rev0 probe shim replaced NO_ARGS with a two-property schema. listTools() derives the advertised list and order from PAGE_ACTIONS, not Object.keys(TOOL_CATALOG).
discoveryFindings.implication: captureTab's schema must describe exactly mode (enum of the two strings, viewport default documented) + elementRef (optional string); tool-catalog.unit.test.ts's captureTab-specific assertions (empty properties, required map) must change in lockstep.

discoveryFindings.finding: src/mcp/server.ts handleToolCall special-cases `if (toolName === 'captureTab') return imageResult(stripDataUrlPrefix(readDataUrl(response.result)))`. imageResult returns `{ content: [{ type:'image', data: base64Png, mimeType:'image/png' }] }`. Every other tool returns textResult(JSON.stringify(result,null,2)). Errors -> textResult(..., true) with isError:true. No size/base64 guard here. readDataUrl returns '' on a shapeless result.
discoveryFindings.implication: The `=== 'captureTab'` branch must be generalised: a real capture still renders as an image block, but a structured too-large / element-not-found / zero-area outcome is detected before the imageResult path and surfaced via textResult with isError set as appropriate; server.unit.test.ts gets coverage for each non-image outcome plus the success case.

discoveryFindings.finding: Signature `withDebuggerSession<T>(tabId: number, label: 'capturing' | 'evaluating' | 'scrolling', run: () => Promise<T>, timeoutMs = CDP_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS): Promise<T>`. The label union is a closed 3-member string-literal union. CDP_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS = 15000. It attaches chrome.debugger '1.3', races run() vs a detach rejection and a timeout, and in finally clears the timeout, deletes the inFlight entry, then detaches (catch noop). One chrome.debugger.onDetach listener registered at construction.
discoveryFindings.implication: The element-rect read and the clip screenshot reuse existing labels ('evaluating' / 'capturing') or add a label literal to this union and its test; the 15s cap and attach/detach lifecycle come for free.

discoveryFindings.finding: In screenshotTab: `await chrome.debugger.sendCommand({tabId}, 'Page.captureScreenshot', { format: 'png' })`. Only format:'png' is passed. Reply parsed by readScreenshotBase64. debugger-ports.unit.test.ts pins the call: `toHaveBeenCalledWith({tabId:7},'Page.captureScreenshot',{format:'png'})`. The rev0 probe shim added an options arg forwarding captureBeyondViewport + clip.
discoveryFindings.implication: Element = add clip:{x,y,width,height,scale}; the captureBeyondViewport branch from the probe shim is removed. DebuggerPorts.captureScreenshot(tabId, options?): Promise<string> keeps an optional options arg for clip only. The pinned unit-test assertion must keep asserting the viewport call sends exactly {format:'png'}.

discoveryFindings.finding: DebuggerPorts.evaluate(tabId, expression): Promise<InPageScriptOutcome> in debugger-ports.ts calls Runtime.evaluate `{ expression, returnByValue:true, awaitPromise:true }` mapped via cdpEvalOutcome to {ok:true,json}/{ok:false,error}. The port already does internal geometry reads: private readScrollMetrics evaluates `({ scrollY, scrollHeight: document.documentElement.scrollHeight, innerHeight, innerWidth })` via the same shape.
discoveryFindings.implication: Measuring an element getBoundingClientRect() is directly doable - reuse public evaluate() or add a private helper mirroring readScrollMetrics/parseScrollMetrics. No new CDP domain. ref->rect resolution runs as a Runtime.evaluate returning the rect JSON.

discoveryFindings.finding: The ref CSS-locator is generated inside the ISOLATED-world injected function in raw.findElement (page-actions.ts ~line 498) by buildRef(el, depth): prefers `#${CSS.escape(id)}` when unique, else recurses up building `${buildRef(parent)} > ${tag}:nth-of-type(${index})`, capped at MAX_REF_DEPTH = 8. clickElement consumes any selector via document.querySelector(selector). findElement re-feeds a ref through document.querySelectorAll(selector).
discoveryFindings.implication: Element-screenshot-by-ref can resolve the rect with document.querySelector(ref).getBoundingClientRect() via CDP evaluate exactly as clickElement/findElement do - no new ref format or handle registry.

discoveryFindings.area: parity surface - change existing action vs add new action

Consumers typed Record<PageAction,...> so tsc enforces completeness: types.ts (Params interface, Result interface, PageActionParams map, PageActionResults map); page-actions.ts (raw handler + guarded map); tool-catalog.ts (TOOL_CATALOG entry). listTools/command-dispatch.ts/guards.ts/server.ts are driven generically off PAGE_ACTIONS/isPageAction and need NO per-action edit. Changing only a Result/Params SHAPE of an existing action touches types.ts, page-actions.ts (1 handler body), tool-catalog.ts (description/schema) - NOT PAGE_ACTIONS, not command-dispatch.ts, not the count tests.
discoveryFindings.implication: Folding into captureTab: no PAGE_ACTIONS/count-test churn (stays 20). Only the captureTab-specific assertions in tool-catalog.unit.test.ts change.

discoveryFindings.finding: src/protocol/actions.unit.test.ts: `expect([...PAGE_ACTIONS]).toEqual([...20 names...])` and `expect(PAGE_ACTIONS.length).toBe(20)`. src/mcp/tool-catalog.unit.test.ts: `Object.keys(TOOL_CATALOG).sort() toEqual [...PAGE_ACTIONS].sort()`, `listTools() toHaveLength(20)`, `names toEqual [...PAGE_ACTIONS]`, a per-action required map assertion, and the 'ping, captureTab, getTabState empty properties' test.

discoveryFindings.finding: tools/chrome-bridge/extension/manifest.json permissions: tabs, activeTab, scripting, storage, alarms, debugger; host_permissions <all_urls>. debugger is already present (added h06 phase 0). README step 13's Verified block asserts `diff extension/manifest.json dist/extension/manifest.json` is empty.
discoveryFindings.implication: Element/clip screenshot needs NO new permission - debugger already covers Page.captureScreenshot with clip and Runtime.evaluate. 'Any new manifest permission' is a red flag the roadmaps require explicit justification for.

discoveryFindings.finding: README.md lists the 20 actions by name twice; 'connected with 20 tools' at line 232 (manual e2e step 3). captureTab e2e step 5: 'Call captureTab - a PNG screenshot comes back as an image block.' Dated Verified blocks: horizon 09 evaluatePage, horizon 12 findElement, horizon 10 scrollPage. The rev0 probe left a phase-0 'COMPLETE - SPLIT VERDICT' block that records the captureBeyondViewport failure and the clip success.
discoveryFindings.implication: A captureTab shape change updates step 5 prose + the captureTab paragraph + adds a new dated Verified block; the count and name lists are untouched (stays 20). The rev0 phase-0 SPLIT-VERDICT block is kept as the record of why full-page was dropped.

discoveryFindings.finding: The only size guards: MAX_EXECUTE_SCRIPT_RESULT_CHARS = 1_000_000 (executeScript + CDP evaluate JSON length); DEFAULT_MAX_CHARS = 200_000 / MAX_READ_LIMIT; MAX_FIND_ELEMENT_MATCHES = 50 / MAX_ELEMENT_TEXT_CHARS = 500. There is NO guard on screenshot byte size, base64 length, or the dataUrl in CaptureTabResult.
discoveryFindings.implication: The screenshot size guard is greenfield - a flat too-large outcome in raw.captureTab, ceiling a single named constant sibling to MAX_EXECUTE_SCRIPT_RESULT_CHARS with a comment citing the ~275KB viewport-PNG baseline. A large element clip can still be big.

discoveryFindings.finding: horizon-12 used 2 phases: Phase 1 = change the action Result shape across the FULL parity surface atomically in one commit (types + both mapped types, raw + guarded handlers, TOOL_CATALOG, edited unit tests + count assertions still green at 20 + a new adversarial test, README prose + one new manual-e2e step), proven complete by tsc; Phase 2 = live-Chrome head-to-head, ending blocked MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING if the environment is unavailable.
discoveryFindings.implication: Element screenshot extends captureTab (not a new action), so build+wire collapses into one phase like h12 phase 1, count stays 20; followed by a live-Chrome verify phase. The rev1 roadmap is exactly this 2-phase shape (the rev0 feasibility gate is now spent).

requiredMaterials.name: Live signed-in Chrome session with the chrome-bridge extension loaded and the devtools relay running
requiredMaterials.whyNeeded: The horizon's success definition (item 7) makes a mandatory live head-to-head verification in a fresh post-rebuild MCP session non-negotiable: element image width/height cross-checked against a measured getBoundingClientRect, the flat too-large guard observed firing on a large element clip, and a post-run debugger-detach check. Cannot be simulated in vitest.
requiredMaterials.acquisitionNote: Run npm start from repo root for the relay, rebuild + reload tools/chrome-bridge/extension unpacked in a real signed-in Chrome, then start a fresh MCP session. Same setup that blocked h9/h11/h12; budget for a --retry in a later fresh session and a MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING close if the environment is unavailable.

requiredMaterials.name: A real scrollable public page and a real large below-the-fold element for the verification target
requiredMaterials.whyNeeded: Item 7 requires the cross-check to run against a real large element (below the fold, getBoundingClientRect well beyond a trivial size) whose measured rect can be compared to the clip-rect capture, and against an element large enough to trip the too-large guard.
requiredMaterials.acquisitionNote: Pick a stable, long, publicly reachable page (no auth wall) at verification time and navigate the sandbox tab to it via navigateTo; use findElement to get a ref for a large table/figure/section; record the URL and the ref in the dated README Verified block. The rev0 probe used en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromium_(web_browser) with table.wikitable.

requiredMaterials.name: CDP Page.captureScreenshot clip + deviceScaleFactor / emulation interaction semantics
requiredMaterials.whyNeeded: Risk items 3 and 4: clip interacts with device-scale-factor so returned pixel dimensions may not equal measured CSS-pixel dimensions (sandbox tab dpr 2). Need the exact contract for how clip.scale and captured pixel dimensions combine so the cross-check reconciliation (measurement x dpr = image, within tolerance) is correct.
requiredMaterials.acquisitionNote: Chrome DevTools Protocol docs for Page.captureScreenshot - external reference, not in repo. Confirm against the actual Chrome build during the live verification; the rev0 probe already observed a working clip crop of the exact element.

requiredMaterials.name: Concrete MCP result-size / image content-block byte limit
requiredMaterials.whyNeeded: Item 4 requires a documented flat guard that keeps the returned PNG within MCP result-size limits. The ~275KB viewport baseline is known but the actual ceiling the guard constant should encode is not established in-repo.
requiredMaterials.acquisitionNote: Determine the effective ceiling empirically during live verification and/or from MCP SDK / host limits; the roadmap's chosen behaviour is a flat too-large outcome carrying measured bytes + the ceiling constant, no downscale.

phases.name: Add viewport and element capture modes to captureTab
phases.goal: In one atomic change across the captureTab parity surface, add a mutually-exclusive two-value mode field (visible viewport | one element by ref) plus an element-ref field, resolve the ref to a CDP clip rect via the existing Runtime.evaluate read path, return width/height/clipped metadata in the result, and add a flat non-throwing guard that turns an oversized returned image into a defined too-large outcome. Full-page / captureBeyondViewport is not in scope (phase-0 probe proved it hangs past the 15s cap or errors CDP -32000 on the unfocused sandbox tab and never returns an image).
phases.rationale: captureTab today takes no arguments and captures only the visible area, and nothing anywhere checks screenshot size. The phase-0 probe proved clip-rect capture composites a genuinely below-the-fold element (table.wikitable at y=4459.77, scrollY 0) on the unfocused sandbox tab in 2058ms with a clean detach, while captureBeyondViewport:true is non-functional there. This phase ships exactly two modes - viewport (default, behaviour unchanged) and element (CDP clip:{x,y,width,height,scale}) - wired through every coupled consumer at once so a missing one is a compile error. PAGE_ACTIONS stays at 20 because the shape changes in place rather than via a new action (h12 precedent).
changes: In protocol/types.ts add to CaptureTabParams one required-with-default mode field of exactly two values (visible viewport / element) and a second elementRef field holding a findElement CSS-locator ref, read only when mode is element; add width, height, clipped (true only in element mode when the element rect was larger than the composited viewport so the returned image is cropped to the viewport, false otherwise), and a too-large marker (measured bytes plus the ceiling) to CaptureTabResult; keep the PageActionParams and PageActionResults map entries in lockstep; remove the probe-only captureBeyondViewport param field entirely.

Give DebuggerPorts.captureScreenshot an optional options arg that passes clip:{x,y,width,height,scale} for element mode (no captureBeyondViewport branch), and update the pinned Page.captureScreenshot unit-test assertion in the same commit so the viewport call is still asserted to send exactly {format:'png'}.

In raw.captureTab read and validate params; for element mode resolve the ref to a rect via a Runtime.evaluate document.querySelector(ref).getBoundingClientRect() read mirroring readScrollMetrics, with defined non-throwing outcomes for no-match, zero-area, and relay/tab-unavailable.

Add a size guard in raw.captureTab that measures the returned base64 length against a documented ceiling constant sibling to MAX_EXECUTE_SCRIPT_RESULT_CHARS and, when exceeded, returns the defined too-large result outcome carrying the measured size and the ceiling; no downscale, no re-capture (a large element clip can still be big).

Replace NO_ARGS with a real inputSchema for captureTab in tool-catalog.ts (mode as an enum of the two exact strings with the viewport default documented, elementRef as an optional string), update the captureTab-specific unit assertions (empty-properties test, required map), update README step 5 prose and the captureTab paragraph, confirm PAGE_ACTIONS stays 20 and the Record<PageAction,...> mapped types still tsc-check, and run npm run verify green.

In mcp/server.ts generalise the handleToolCall toolName === 'captureTab' branch so a successful capture still renders as an MCP image content block, but a structured too-large / element-not-found / zero-area outcome is detected before the imageResult path and surfaced via textResult (JSON of the outcome) with isError set as appropriate; add server.unit.test.ts coverage asserting each non-image outcome round-trips as a text/error block and the success case still yields an image block.

rubric.label: Ref resolution has defined non-throwing outcomes
rubric.ruleStatement: In element mode, resolving the CSS-locator ref to a clip rect returns a structured outcome for every miss instead of throwing or hanging. 10 = no-match, zero-area, and relay/tab-unavailable each produce a distinct named non-throwing result with enough detail to act on, all covered by tests; 8 = all three cases handled non-throwing and tested, messages adequate; minScore 6 = no-match and zero-area handled non-throwing and tested, tab-unavailable at least not an unhandled throw.
passCriteria: page-actions.ts element-mode path resolves the ref via a Runtime.evaluate document.querySelector(ref).getBoundingClientRect() read (grep confirms getBoundingClientRect, not a new CDP DOM.getBoxModel dependency)
A unit test asserts that when querySelector returns null the result is a defined outcome object (e.g. element-not-found) and no exception propagates
A unit test asserts that a matched element with width 0 or height 0 yields a distinct zero-area outcome, not a CDP call with a degenerate clip
A unit test asserts the relay/tab-unavailable path returns a structured error result rather than rejecting
The three failure outcomes are distinguishable by a discriminant field (not the same generic error string)
failureExamples: querySelector-null path throws a plain Error that the raw handler does not catch, so the MCP call returns a stack trace instead of a structured result
A careful implementation returns element-not-found correctly but treats a zero-area element as a valid 0x0 clip and forwards it to Page.captureScreenshot, which errors CDP -32000
no-match and zero-area both return `{ ok: false, error: 'could not capture element' }` with no way to tell them apart

rubric.label: Too-large guard is flat, non-throwing, and informative
rubric.ruleStatement: An oversized returned image produces a defined too-large result carrying measured bytes and the ceiling constant, with no downscale or re-capture. 10 = ceiling is a named exported/documented constant sibling to MAX_EXECUTE_SCRIPT_RESULT_CHARS, outcome carries both measured size and ceiling, guard applies to both modes, and tests cover just-over and just-under; 8 = constant documented, outcome carries both numbers, one boundary test; minScore 6 = guard exists, is non-throwing, and returns something identifying the size problem.
passCriteria: A single ceiling constant is defined near MAX_EXECUTE_SCRIPT_RESULT_CHARS with a comment explaining the value, and the guard compares base64 length against it (grep for the constant name used in both places)
When exceeded, raw.captureTab returns the too-large result variant containing the measured size and the ceiling value as numbers - not a thrown error, not a truncated image
No code path downscales, changes scale, or re-invokes Page.captureScreenshot after an over-limit measurement
A unit test feeds a mock base64 payload longer than the ceiling and asserts the too-large outcome with both numbers populated
A unit test feeds a payload just under the ceiling and asserts a normal image result
The guard runs for element mode as well as viewport mode
failureExamples: The guard throws `new Error('screenshot too large')` instead of returning a structured outcome, breaking the non-throwing contract

A developer measures `dataUrl.length` including the `data:image/png;base64,` prefix against a raw-bytes ceiling, so the reported measured size is off and the boundary test is calibrated to the wrong quantity
The too-large outcome reports only a boolean `clipped`/`tooLarge` flag with no measured size or ceiling, so the caller cannot tell how far over it was

rubric.label: Viewport CDP call stays exactly {format:'png'}
rubric.ruleStatement: The viewport (default) mode still calls Page.captureScreenshot with exactly {format:'png'} and the pinned assertion is updated in the same commit to keep proving that, while element mode adds only a clip. 10 = viewport params byte-identical to before, element-mode test asserts the exact clip shape {x,y,width,height,scale} and absence of captureBeyondViewport; 8 = viewport assertion intact and passing, element clip asserted; minScore 7 = viewport call still exactly {format:'png'} and its test green.
passCriteria: debugger-ports.unit.test.ts still contains an assertion that the viewport call sends exactly {format:'png'} (deep-equal, not partial match) and it passes
The assertion was edited (not deleted or `.skip`-ed) in this phase's diff if it moved - `git log -p` shows it changed in the same commit as debugger-ports.ts
An element-mode test asserts Page.captureScreenshot receives `clip: {x, y, width, height, scale}` with scale present and no captureBeyondViewport key
No test uses it.skip, it.only, relaxed matchers (objectContaining where equality was used before), or an increased timeout to accommodate the change
failureExamples: The pinned test is changed to `expect.objectContaining({ format: 'png' })` so it would no longer catch an accidental extra param on the viewport call
Element mode works but its test only checks that captureScreenshot was called, never asserting the clip rect values, so a swapped x/y would pass
The viewport assertion is left untouched and now fails because the implementation always passes a `clip: undefined` key, and the developer bumps the test timeout hoping it is flakiness

rubric.label: MCP server routes image vs non-image outcomes
rubric.ruleStatement: mcp/server.ts renders a real capture as an image content block and every structured non-image outcome (too-large, element-not-found, zero-area) as a text/error block, with test coverage for each branch. 10 = every non-image outcome round-trips as text with isError set appropriately AND the success path still yields an image block AND the branch no longer hard-codes an assumption that captureTab always produces an image; 8 = all outcomes covered and tested; minScore 6 = success yields image, at least the too-large outcome yields a non-image text block, both tested.
passCriteria: The `toolName === 'captureTab'` branch in server.ts checks the result shape and only takes the imageResult/readDataUrl path when the result actually carries image data
server.unit.test.ts asserts the success case returns an MCP image content block
server.unit.test.ts asserts the too-large outcome returns a text block (JSON of the outcome) with isError set
server.unit.test.ts asserts element-not-found and zero-area outcomes return text/error blocks rather than attempting image rendering
readDataUrl/imageResult is never called with a non-image outcome (verifiable: a test with a too-large mock does not hit the image path - e.g. spy asserts not-called)
failureExamples: The branch still calls `readDataUrl(result.dataUrl)` unconditionally; for a too-large outcome `dataUrl` is undefined and the server throws or emits an empty image block
A developer routes too-large to a text block but leaves element-not-found flowing through the image path because only one failure variant was considered
Non-image outcomes are returned as text but always with isError:false, so an MCP client treats element-not-found as a successful call

phases.healerHint: The most likely miss is an unhandled failure path - a null querySelector, zero-area element, or missing dataUrl reaching Page.captureScreenshot or readDataUrl and throwing; wrap each into its named structured outcome and route it to a text/error block before the image path.

phases.name: Verify viewport and element captures live in Chrome
phases.goal: In a fresh post-rebuild MCP session against real signed-in Chrome, capture both modes on a real long page - visible viewport, and a single large below-the-fold element by ref - cross-check the returned element image pixel width/height against a CDP evaluatePage getBoundingClientRect measurement (DPR reconciled), confirm the flat too-large guard returns its defined outcome on a genuinely large element clip, confirm no orphaned debugger attachment, and record a dated Verified README block; end the horizon MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING if the live environment is unavailable.
phases.rationale: The binding project rule (horizon-02 decision) is that any horizon changing the extension closes only after a real end-to-end Chrome check. The phase-0 probe already proved clip capture composites off-screen content on the unfocused sandbox tab; this phase verifies the shipped captureTab viewport and element modes end to end and performs the numeric returned-image-vs-measurement cross-check that phase 0 structurally could not do, now that CaptureTabResult carries width/height.
changes: Rebuild and reload the chrome-bridge extension, start a fresh MCP session, and navigate the sandbox tab to a stable long public page.

Call captureTab in element mode with a ref for a large below-the-fold element and confirm the returned image width/height track its CDP evaluatePage getBoundingClientRect (record both number pairs and reconcile devicePixelRatio); call visible-viewport mode and confirm the default is unchanged (image at viewport size).

Confirm the flat size guard returns the defined too-large outcome (measured bytes plus ceiling) on a genuinely large element clip, and that no chrome.debugger attachment is left orphaned on the sandbox tab after the run.

Add a dated Verified block and a new manual-e2e step to the README recording the target URL, the element ref, the measured-vs-returned dimensions, and the guard/detach observations; leave the horizon MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING if the live environment is unavailable, naming the blocker and the manual steps to close it.
inputs: stage1-analysis success definition item 7 (mandatory live head-to-head, CDP cross-check), narrowed to viewport + element
phase-0 probe: the numeric returned-image-vs-measurement cross-check is deferred here where CaptureTabResult.width/height exists
live signed-in Chrome session with the extension loaded and the relay running
phases.expectedResult: A dated Verified README block recording the viewport and element captures cross-checked against CDP dimension measurements plus the too-large guard firing on a large element clip and a clean post-run debugger-detach check, or a MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING note naming the blocker if the environment was unavailable.

rubric.label: Dated Verified block or honest pending note exists
rubric.ruleStatement: The deliverable in tools/chrome-bridge/README.md is EITHER a Verified block carrying a concrete calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) and a manual-e2e step for the two capture modes, OR a MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING note that names the specific live-environment blocker and lists the manual steps to close it. Scale: 10 = a reader can tell at a glance which mode the close is in, the date/blocker is unambiguous, and the block is self-contained; 8 = block present, dated or blocker-named, minor vagueness; minScore = the block exists and is honestly one mode or the other, not a hand-waved 'effectively verified' claim.
passCriteria: Open tools/chrome-bridge/README.md and locate a section headed 'Verified' (or equivalent) added for horizon 13, OR a note containing the literal token MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING.
If Verified: it contains an ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) that is plausibly recent, not a placeholder like 'YYYY-MM-DD' or 'TBD'.

If pending: the text names a concrete blocker (e.g. 'relay not running on ws://localhost:8765', 'MCP tool catalog frozen without the capture-mode field', 'no signed-in Chrome tab') AND lists the manual steps an operator would run to complete the check.
The block does not claim the check passed while also admitting it was not actually run ('effectively verified', 'should work', 'verified by unit tests').
failureExamples: README has a new prose paragraph saying 'captureTab was tested and works' with no date, no URL, no numbers.
A Verified block dated 'YYYY-MM-DD' with the placeholder never filled in.

Plausible-implementation miss: developer adds a genuine Verified block but forgets to include the date line because the surrounding README uses relative wording ('recently verified'), so the close cannot be audited against the horizon timeline.

rubric.label: Returned element image dimensions vs CDP measurement, both numbers recorded
rubric.ruleStatement: For the element-mode capture, the deliverable records TWO explicit numeric width/height pairs - the returned CaptureTabResult image pixel dimensions and the CDP evaluatePage getBoundingClientRect measurement - and shows they reconcile once devicePixelRatio is applied. Scale: 10 = both raw pairs, the DPR value, and the arithmetic reconciliation (measurement x dpr = image, within a stated tolerance) are all written out; 8 = both pairs and the dpr-2 reconciliation stated, tolerance implied; minScore = both number pairs are recorded as actual observed values (not 'matched') and DPR 2 is explicitly accounted for.
passCriteria: The block states the returned image width and height in pixels as concrete integers (e.g. '1024 x 3480').
The block states the getBoundingClientRect width and height from CDP evaluatePage as concrete numbers (e.g. '512 x 1740').

The block names the sandbox tab devicePixelRatio (expected: 2) and shows the reconciliation: CSS-pixel measurement multiplied by DPR equals the returned image dimensions, within a stated pixel tolerance.
The element ref string used (the CSS-locator from findElement) is quoted verbatim in the block.
The target page URL is a stable public page and is recorded.
failureExamples: Block says 'returned image dimensions matched the element bounding box' with no numbers.
Only the returned image dimensions are recorded; the CDP measurement is described as 'roughly the same'.

Plausible-implementation miss: developer records both pairs but eyeballs the DPR - notes the image is 'about 2x the box, as expected' without writing the dpr value or doing the multiplication, so a 1.5x or off-by-a-scrollbar discrepancy would pass unnoticed.

rubric.label: Viewport-default mode confirmed at viewport size
rubric.ruleStatement: The deliverable records that a captureTab call with no mode argument (or explicit visible-viewport mode) returned an image whose dimensions equal the sandbox tab's viewport size times DPR, confirming the default behaviour is unchanged. Scale: 10 = returned image dimensions plus the viewport innerWidth/innerHeight plus DPR reconciliation all recorded; 8 = returned dimensions recorded and stated to equal viewport size; minScore = the default-mode call is shown to have run live and produced a viewport-sized (not element) image.
passCriteria: The block shows a captureTab invocation that passes no capture-mode field, or explicitly the visible-viewport value.
The returned image width/height for that call are recorded as integers.
The block states the sandbox tab viewport size (window.innerWidth/innerHeight) and notes the returned image is that size times DPR (expected 2).
The block explicitly notes full-page mode is not offered (only two modes exist).
failureExamples: Block only covers the element capture and says nothing about the default viewport mode.
Block says 'default mode still works' with no dimensions.

Plausible-implementation miss: developer captures the viewport shot and records its pixel size but does not record the viewport innerWidth/innerHeight, treating 'looks like the visible area' as sufficient - so a regression that captured a stale cached frame at a coincidentally similar height would not be caught.

rubric.label: Result-size guard observed returning its defined too-large outcome
rubric.ruleStatement: The deliverable records that the flat result-size guard was observed firing on a GENUINELY large element clip during this live run, returning its defined structured outcome carrying measured bytes and the ceiling constant - not merely asserted from code reading or unit tests. Scale: 10 = the triggering element/ref, the measured byte count, and the ceiling constant value are all quoted from the live outcome, plus a note that a normal-size clip did NOT trip it; 8 = the outcome shape (measured bytes + ceiling) is quoted from a live large-clip call; minScore = the block states the guard was exercised against a real large element in this session and returned the too-large outcome, with the measured bytes recorded.
passCriteria: The block identifies a specific large element (ref or description) whose clip exceeded the ceiling.
The recorded outcome is the flat too-large result (not an exception / not a truncated image), and includes the measured byte size as a number.
The ceiling constant value is recorded and matches the constant defined in the source.
The block distinguishes this from static verification - wording makes clear the guard was actually triggered live, e.g. an actual tool response is quoted.
failureExamples: Block says 'the size guard is covered by unit tests in page-actions.unit.test.ts' with no live observation.
Block says the guard 'would fire' on large elements without having triggered it.

Plausible-implementation miss: the developer's chosen 'large' below-the-fold element compresses to a PNG under the ceiling, the guard never fires, and they record 'guard did not trigger, element was within limits' and move on - without hunting for an element genuinely large enough to exercise the guard, leaving the too-large path unverified live.

rubric.label: Post-run debugger-detach check recorded
rubric.ruleStatement: The deliverable records an explicit post-run check that no chrome.debugger attachment is left on the sandbox tab after all captures completed, describing HOW it was checked. Scale: 10 = the check method is named (e.g. chrome.debugger.getTargets output, absence of the 'DevTools is debugging this tab' banner, a bridge diagnostic) and the observed clean result is quoted, plus checked after an error/guard-trip path too; 8 = method named and clean result recorded for the happy path; minScore = the block states the detach check was performed after the run and found no orphaned attachment, with at least a one-line method.
passCriteria: The block contains a sentence explicitly about debugger/CDP attachment state after the run.
It names how attachment was checked (getTargets, the yellow debugging banner, a bridge/MCP status call, chrome://inspect).
It records the observed result as clean (no attached debuggee for the sandbox tab).
Ideally the check is noted as run after the too-large-guard path, not only after a successful capture.
failureExamples: No mention of debugger attachment anywhere in the block.
Block says 'debugger detaches automatically' - an assumption, not an observation.

Plausible-implementation miss: developer checks the tab looks normal and there is no debugging banner after the successful viewport capture, records 'no orphaned attachment', but never re-checks after the guard-trip / error path where a detach in a non-happy branch is most likely to be missed.

rubric.label: Fresh post-rebuild MCP session evidenced
rubric.ruleStatement: The deliverable makes clear the verification ran against a freshly rebuilt and reloaded extension in a new MCP session - not a stale build or a carried-over session - OR, in the pending case, identifies exactly this (stale catalog / no fresh session) as the blocker. Scale: 10 = rebuild command, extension reload, and new-session start are each noted with enough detail to reproduce, and the captureTab tool signature seen by the session is confirmed to include the new capture-mode field; 8 = rebuild + reload + fresh session stated; minScore = the block asserts a fresh post-rebuild session was used and the mode field was available to it.
passCriteria: The block states the extension was rebuilt (names the build command or output dir) and reloaded in Chrome before the run.
The block states a fresh MCP session was started for this verification.

The block confirms the captureTab tool as exposed to that session accepts the capture-mode field added in the dependency phase (e.g. an element-mode call succeeded rather than erroring on an unknown argument).
If MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING: a frozen/stale MCP tool catalog that does not expose the mode field is explicitly named as the blocker where that is the cause.
failureExamples: Block records captures but never mentions rebuilding or reloading the extension.
Element-mode call is shown but there is no evidence the running build actually contained phase-1's changes.

Plausible-implementation miss: developer runs the check in the MCP session already open from earlier work, the captureTab schema is the pre-phase-1 one, the mode argument is silently ignored, the capture returns a viewport shot for both calls, and the numbers happen to look plausible - recorded as a pass because a fresh session was assumed rather than started.

phases.healerHint: The most likely failure is a hand-waved close - captures described as 'matching' with no recorded number pairs, no live guard trigger, or no debugger-detach check; fix it by re-running against a fresh post-rebuild session and writing the actual returned vs CDP width/height integers, the DPR-2 reconciliation arithmetic, the too-large outcome's measured bytes, and the detach-check method into the dated README block, or by switching to an honest MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING note that names the exact environment blocker.

successCriteria: The narrowed seven-part success definition in analysis.successDefinition (viewport-default + single-element clip screenshots; full-page explicitly out).

Add viewport and element capture modes to captureTab: captureTab accepts the two-value mode field plus an element ref, returns width/height/clipped metadata or a defined too-large outcome, npm run verify green, PAGE_ACTIONS still 20.

Verify viewport and element captures live in Chrome: a dated Verified README block recording the viewport and element captures cross-checked against CDP getBoundingClientRect measurements (DPR reconciled), the too-large guard firing on a large element clip, and a clean post-run debugger-detach check - or an honest MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING note naming the blocker.

The element-clip capability is delivered as one atomic parity-surface change (phase 1) and closed by the phase-2 live head-to-head; protocol/actions.ts (PAGE_ACTIONS) is verified UNCHANGED at 20 entries, not edited.

Full-page / captureBeyondViewport is not shipped this horizon and is recorded (decisions.md + discoveries.md) as infeasible on the unfocused sandbox tab, deferred behind a render-the-tab prerequisite.
deferred: Full-page / beyond-viewport (captureBeyondViewport) screenshots - dropped after the rev0 phase-0 live probe (2026-09-04) proved Page.captureScreenshot({captureBeyondViewport:true}) hangs past the 15s withDebuggerSession cap or errors CDP -32000 on the deliberately-unfocused sandbox tab and never returns an image; deferred behind a 'briefly render the sandbox tab' prerequisite.
A general focus / briefly render the sandbox tab capability - the prerequisite full-page capture now sits behind; its own future horizon.
A scroll-and-stitch client-side full-page fallback if a render-the-tab approach is not wanted - a different mechanism, its own replanned approach.
Network response-body capture for text/JSON (blocker #4) - a separate deferred capability the user did not pick.
clickElement / clickAt by visible text or ARIA role and a fuller synthetic pointer/keyboard event sequence (blocker #5) - a separate deferred slice, unrelated to screenshot capture.
Reviving the horizon-5 DOM page-model / bounding-box snapshot action - planned-but-never-executed and possibly superseded by h12 findElement; not this horizon's slice.

Deleting the dead active-tab surface (queryActiveTab / captureVisibleTab / NO_ACTIVE_TAB / redundant activeTab permission) - the brief says keep horizon 13 to one deliverable and give that cleanup its own horizon.
Verifying the capability from Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, or Cursor - the h4 decision binds all hand-verification to Claude Code for the life of the project.
PDF export, JPEG/quality knobs, or other CDP capture formats/options beyond png + clip - not asked for; format proliferation is speculative.
Migrating boky's own extension/relay/MCP onto the chrome-bridge tool - the vision's h1 decision forbids it.
Changing the MCP result-rendering layer to add a generic size guard for all tools - any size bound added here is scoped to the screenshot result; a cross-tool cap is a separate open question.

Downscale-and-retry / re-capture-at-lower-scale behaviour for an oversized screenshot payload - per the rev0 user redirect the size guard stays flat: an oversized base64 payload returns a defined non-throwing too-large outcome.
revisionReason: REPLAN verdict revise-phases (2026-09-04): the rev0 phase-0 live probe proved CDP Page.captureScreenshot({captureBeyondViewport:true}) is non-functional on the deliberately-unfocused sandbox tab (hangs past the 15s withDebuggerSession cap or errors CDP -32000, never returns an image), while single-element clip capture composites a below-the-fold element cleanly. Full-page / beyond-viewport is dropped from this horizon and deferred behind a render-the-tab prerequisite. Phase 0 (probe) is removed - its feasibility question is answered and recorded in discoveries.md/blockers.md. Phases 1 and 2 are replaced: the mode enum narrows from three values to two (visible viewport | element), DebuggerPorts.captureScreenshot loses the captureBeyondViewport branch, and the live verification narrows to the element-image-vs-getBoundingClientRect cross-check (now possible because CaptureTabResult carries width/height) plus the too-large guard firing on a large element clip. The objective and successDefinition are narrowed accordingly; a corrective decisions.md line records the falsification of the 2026-09-04 captureBeyondViewport decision. Previous content preserved at horizon-13-full-page-element-screenshots-roadmap.rev0.json.
